identity.title: Data Channels
identity.subTitle: Part 1: Streaming over an established SecureChannel
identity._comment_namespaceIsSubset: This document adds Nodes to the base OPC UA namespace rather than owning one, so its UANodeSet holds only those additions. Stating False here would claim the file contains the whole base namespace.
introduction: A data channel is a logical, flow-controlled, bidirectional stream of opaque bytes carried on a SecureChannel that is already open. Several channels are multiplexed onto that one connection, each with its own credit, its own delivery mode and its own lifetime, so continuous content flows over the connection a Client already holds instead of over a second protocol beside it.

OPC UA has no such primitive today. Secure Conversation carries only the request-response message types, so continuous data has to be faked — polled through file transfer, or pushed out of the request-response path into PubSub, which changes the addressing, the security and the deployment model at the same time.

This document defines the missing primitive: a frame, the flow control and scheduling rules that govern it, a Service Set that opens and closes channels, and the Nodes that let a Client discover which parts of an address space can be one end of one. It is a proposed addition to the base OPC UA namespace, not a new companion namespace.
identity.draftBanner: PROVISIONAL WORKING DRAFT — not normative, not endorsed by the OPC Foundation. The document number, the Mantis project identifier and every NodeId in this document are placeholders; the OPC Foundation assigns the real values.

_comment_useCases: The template requires a Use cases clause and this document has no material shaped like one: its worked session and its when-to-use-which guidance are Annexes C and E and stay there. This clause summarises them.
useCases: A data channel is for content that is continuous, ordered within itself, and too large or too frequent to carry as a sequence of Service responses. Three families of use case motivate it.

Media. A camera, a microphone or a screen source exposes an encoded stream — H.264 video, Opus audio — as a data channel, and a Client that has already authenticated to the Server subscribes to it without opening a second connection to a second protocol with a second set of credentials. Annex C works one such session through in full, including the control channel that carries the pan, tilt and zoom commands alongside the media.

Bulk and continuous transfer. A recorder, a log or a firmware image is read as a stream rather than polled block by block through file transfer, so the Server controls the rate with credit instead of the Client controlling it with a polling interval.

Loss-tolerant telemetry. A source whose value is only useful when it is fresh — a waveform, a position, a pose — is carried in a delivery mode that permits the Server to discard rather than to queue, so a slow consumer degrades instead of accumulating latency.

A data channel is not a replacement for a Subscription, for file transfer or for PubSub, each of which remains the better answer to the problem it was designed for. Annex E sets out which mechanism suits which shape of problem.
_comment_termsFrom: The combined document has no terms clause; its terms are defined in the Part 3 erratum it merges. Pointing at that file keeps one source of truth, where copying the definitions into this config would let them drift.
